clue.text: Weak artist's a slovenly creature

parts.note: droopy means limp, lacking strength
read as 'artists': people who draw are drawers

explanation.surface: A feeble painter turns out to be a scruffy sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: 'artist's' stands for 'artists', drawers being people who draw. DROOPY DRAWERS is a British nickname for an untidy person, and drawers also means old-fashioned knickers, which sets up the underwear theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy drawers is a jocular British name for a sloppy, untidy person whose clothes hang badly.

clue.text: See 1
Old Tibetans may be seen as reluctant to change

indicators.note: the letters of Tibetans may be seen rearranged as something else

explanation.surface: A claim that elderly people from Tibet are set in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: O for 'Old' comes first, then the letters of TIBETANS rearranged as BSTINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinate is stubborn and will not alter their views or behaviour.

clue.text: Swimmer's hair getting cut back on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top places this piece above the next
back says the word for cut is read the other way round

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A swimmer whose hair is being trimmed short at the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer is a fish, though the surface pictures a person; Jackson Pollock the American painter also belongs to the artists' theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollock is a sea fish of the cod family, so it is a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Trench restricts spring expedition

indicators.note: the trench word hems in the spring word, holding it inside

parts.note: a ditch is a trench
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A trench hemming in a water source holds up an exploring party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' here means speed and promptness, not a journey: the surface pushes the travelling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch and expedition both mean speed or promptness in getting something done.

clue.text: 30's partner almost part of one's group

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: 30 across is EGRESS, a way out; its natural partner is ingress, a way in

explanation.surface: Someone's mate is nearly a member of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's group' points to 1 across: the drawers, i.e. artists. INGRES the French painter is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter, so he belongs among the artists of the theme.

clue.text: Olympic Association contains member of one's group

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within their letters across the gap

explanation.surface: A sports body includes one of the members of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's group' is 1 across, the drawers or artists; Pablo Picasso is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso was a Spanish painter and sculptor, making him a member of the artists' group.

clue.text: Bikini Atoll's first insect returns

indicators.note: returns means the letters run back the other way
first takes the opening letter of Atoll

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: An insect comes back to the Pacific atoll of Bikini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' looks like the atoll; it is the swimsuit. A then GNAT is AGNAT, and 'returns' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a type of brief bikini or underpants with narrow sides, fitting the underwear theme.

clue.text: Problem keeping bishop in part of one's group

indicators.note: the problem word keeps the bishop letter held inside it

parts.note: to be in a hole is to have a problem
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A difficulty involving a clergyman within a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's group' is 1 across, the drawers or artists; Hans Holbein was a German portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Holbein the Younger was a Renaissance painter, so he is one of the artists in the theme group.

clue.text: Sailor working out in clearing

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
solving means working out

explanation.surface: A seaman exercising in a forest glade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' and 'clearing' suggest exercise and a woodland space; clearing really means freeing from blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to declare them free of guilt, clearing their name.

clue.text: Police Captain possesses a very cool head

indicators.note: the two words possess the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is admirably unflappable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a very cool head' sounds like calmness; it is the frozen covering on top of a polar region or mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent mass of ice on the top of land, literally a frozen head covering.

clue.text: Cut tin and aluminium

parts.note: a can is a tin
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Instructions to slice up metal sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb; it is a noun, an old word for an artificial waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut is a man-made watercourse, the traditional British boatmen's term for a canal.

clue.text: Is lyrical piece on recording part of a series?

indicators.note: on means the later pieces follow after the recording

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Asking whether a poem on a record belongs to a set.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment of a broadcast serial or a run of related events.

clue.text: Trap revolved around getting suspect seen outside

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go outside, wrapping round the other piece
suspect suggests the letters of seen are not to be trusted as they stand
around turns the word for revolved back on itself

parts.note: ran can mean went round, as a machine runs or revolves

explanation.surface: A suspicious-looking person spotted outside a revolving door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolved' gives a past-tense verb, ran in the sense of turned, as wheels run; 'around' then reverses it rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a snare, so it means to trap.

clue.text: Station one can visit for small fare

definitions.text: Station one can visit for small fare

parts.words: Station one can visit for small fare
parts.note: fare suggests a train ticket at a station, but it is food: a place offering light meals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' and 'fare' point to railways; the station is a counter and the small fare is light food.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar is a counter or café where light meals and refreshments are bought.

clue.text: Petrifying woman?

parts.note: petrifying normally means terrifying, but here it means literally turning people to stone

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'petrifying' is meant literally: in Greek myth a glance from Medusa and her sisters turned onlookers to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a Gorgon is a snake-haired female monster whose gaze turns people to stone; the word also means a frightening woman.

clue.text: Female scout cast Gielgud in role originally

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
originally takes the first letter of each of in and role

explanation.surface: A casting director puts actor John Gielgud in a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like theatre casting but it is the anagram signal over GIELGUD plus I and R. Gielgud was a great English stage actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Girl Guide is a member of the Guides, the girls' branch of the scouting movement.

clue.text: Scene involving centre halves in familiar feud

indicators.note: the central half of each word is kept: the middle four letters of familiar and the middle two of feud

explanation.surface: A football report about central defenders caught up in a long-running quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre halves' sounds like football defenders; it means the middle half of each word: MILI from FAMILIAR and EU from FEUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's social setting or environment, the scene they move in.

clue.text: Thrashes Muttley at the beginning in Wacky Races

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
at the beginning takes only the first letter of Muttley

explanation.surface: Muttley the cartoon dog appears at the start of the Wacky Races cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wacky Races is a Hanna-Barbera cartoon featuring the dog Muttley; 'Wacky' is the anagram signal over M plus RACES.
explanation.definitionFit: To cream an opponent is a slang way of saying to beat them heavily.

clue.text: Old woman stops to phone man in one's group

indicators.note: the old woman word plugs the gap inside the phone word, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: to call is to phone
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman halts to make a call to a member of her circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's group' is 1 across, the drawers or artists; Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a modernist painter, so he is a man among the theme's artists.

clue.text: Sea mist swirled around painter

indicators.note: letters that are swirled about are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sea fog drifts round an artist at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist celebrated for his bold use of colour.

clue.text: Red-headed lady losing heart without confidence

parts.note: ginger describes red hair

indicators.note: the lady word loses its central letters

explanation.surface: A red-haired woman becomes downcast and unsure of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' sounds like despair; it removes the middle AD from LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act gingerly is to move cautiously and tentatively, without assurance.

clue.text: Part for violin one made using thin strips of material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the lowest string on a violin, tuned to G

definitions.text: one made using thin strips of material
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a minimal undergarment made of narrow strips of fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part for violin' suggests a musical part in a score; it is a physical part, one of the instrument's strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The G string is the violin's lowest string and also a skimpy undergarment of thin strips, part of the underwear theme.

clue.text: Something found in youngster's yellowing underwear?

definitions.text: Something found in youngster's yellowing underwear?

parts.words: Something found in youngster's yellowing underwear?
parts.note: it looks like a stain in old pants, but the letter Y is found at the front of both youngster's and yellowing

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as Y FRONTS: Y is what fronts 'youngster's' and 'yellowing'. As a whole it is a type of men's briefs with an inverted-Y seam, so it is underwear too.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's or boys' briefs with a front opening shaped like an upside-down Y.

clue.text: What could be made from synthetic fibres?

definitions.text: What could be made from synthetic fibres?

indicators.note: synthetic means artificially put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Wondering what garment man-made fibres could be woven into.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of FIBRES can be made into the answer, and underpants can be made from nylon.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are short close-fitting underpants, often made of man-made fabric.

clue.text: One listens primarily to upmarket radio plays

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving into a new order
primarily takes the first letters of to and upmarket

explanation.surface: A listener tunes chiefly to highbrow radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radio plays' looks like a phrase about drama; 'plays' is the anagram signal over T, U and RADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor, from Latin for hearer, is a listener, such as one attending a lecture.

clue.text: Member of one's group earned right to entertain king and queen

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the earlier letters hold the royal letter inside

parts.note: what you have earned is your due
R stands for both Rex (king) and Regina (queen)

explanation.surface: A club member has earned the right to host royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: One R serves for both 'king and queen', as R abbreviates both Rex and Regina. 'one's group' is 1 across, the artists; Albrecht Dürer was a German painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and printmaker, one of the artists in the theme.

clue.text: Number in football team, for example

indicators.note: in places the example letters inside the team's name

parts.note: Inter is Inter Milan, the Italian football club
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A figure for how many players make up a soccer side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number in football team' suggests a player's shirt number; INTER is Inter Milan, an Italian club.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part.

clue.text: Artist recalled artist's work hanging on wall

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are taken in reverse

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist
RA's, the possessive of RA

explanation.surface: A painter remembered a fellow painter's picture on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work hanging on wall' suggests a painting; it is a woven tapestry, named after the French town of Arras.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich tapestry used as a wall hanging, like the one Polonius hides behind in Hamlet.

clue.text: Learning issue involves character associated with Reading University

indicators.note: the issue word involves, taking within it, the other letters

parts.note: an edition is one issue of a publication
R is the letter of reading, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A news item about a figure linked to the University of Reading in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the English town with its university; 'Reading' gives R, the first of the three Rs, and 'University' gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, the knowledge gained through extensive study.

clue.text: Great letter mentioned distribution of gifts

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: large means great; S is a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An impressive letter refers to the handing out of presents.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'large S' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity in bestowing money or presents, especially on a grand scale.

clue.text: Return to former state only after leader's exit

indicators.note: only what comes after the first letter is kept, the leader dropping out

parts.note: to regress is to return to an earlier state

explanation.surface: Going back to how things were, only after the boss has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's exit' reads as the boss leaving, but 'exit' is the definition and the leader is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is the act of going out or a way out, a formal synonym.
